passage:
Three days before the first paper, Nihal opened his phone and looked at the racing game he played every night. He pressed and held the icon, and deleted it. Then, before lights out, he unplugged his charger and walked to Parth's bed.

"Keep this till seven."

"Seriously?" said Parth. "Your phone is at eleven percent. It'll die by midnight."

"That's the plan."

The first night Nihal lay awake wanting to check something, anything. The second night he read organic chemistry until sleep came. On the morning of the paper he collected his charger, and his phone showed forty-four unread messages that could wait.

qa.q: To whom did Nihal give the charger?
qa.a: Nihal gave the charger to Parth.

qa.q: What was Nihal feeling on the first night?
qa.a: Nihal felt restless and tempted, lying awake wanting to check something.

qa.q: What could Nihal do if the phone is needed in an emergency at night?
qa.a: Nihal could agree with Parth that the charger comes back for a real need, so that the rule bends without breaking.

qa.q: How might Parth feel about keeping the charger?
qa.a: Parth might feel a bit amused and doubtful, judging from "Seriously?", but still willing to help.

grounding: Shows a student before exams deleting a game and handing the charger to a roommate at night so distraction is harder than study.

passage: Two weeks before semester exams, Vishal looked at the screen-time report on his phone: five hours a day, mostly one racing game. His classmate Nazia, sitting next to him in the canteen, whistled. "That's a part-time job." Back in his room at the hostel in Bengaluru, Vishal did two things. He deleted the game, not just logged out. Then he handed his charger to his roommate, Abhay. "Keep this at night. Give it back at seven in the morning, even if I beg." Abhay grinned and tucked it into his own drawer. The first night Vishal reached for his phone at eleven, saw the battery at 12 percent, sighed and opened his circuits notes instead. By the end of the week his notes were finally complete.

qa.q: How many hours a day was Vishal spending on his phone?
qa.a: Five hours a day, mostly one racing game.

qa.q: How did Vishal feel when he reached for his phone at eleven the first night?
qa.a: He felt tempted and a little frustrated, sighing when he saw the low battery, before turning to his notes.

qa.q: What else could Vishal do to make study the easy choice?
qa.a: Keep his books open on the desk at night and study in the library, where the game isn't even on his mind.

qa.q: How might Abhay see his role?
qa.a: Abhay seems amused and willing to help, taking the job of charger-keeper seriously.

grounding: A student before exams deletes a game and hands his charger to his roommate at night, making distraction harder than study.

passage:
"Akash, can you do me a strange favour?"
"Depends."
"Take my charger every night at ten. Give it back after breakfast."
"Why?"
Pradeep held up his phone. "I just deleted the video game. But if the phone's charged, I'll find something else. Exams start in twelve days."
"You deleted it? The one you've been playing since first year?"
"Gone. I'll reinstall it after the last paper."
"And if you ask me for the charger at midnight?"
"Say no. Even if I say it's urgent."
Akash laughed and held out his hand. "Fine. I'm keeping it in my cupboard."
That night, at eleven, Pradeep picked up his phone out of habit. Eight percent. He put it down and opened his notes.
"Good choice," Akash said from his bed, without looking up.

qa.q: When does Pradeep ask Akash to return the charger?
What does Pradeep's 'Say no, even if I say it's urgent' suggest about how he feels?
qa.a: He is worried about his own weak moments and wants a firm guard, knowing he'll be tempted.

qa.q: What could Pradeep do if he starts using a laptop for games instead?
qa.a: Ask Akash to keep the laptop charger too, or study in the library where he doesn't bring it.

qa.q: How does Akash see Pradeep's request?
qa.a: Akash finds it funny at first but respects it, and even cheers him on from his bed.

grounding: A student deletes a game and gives his charger to his roommate at night so distraction is harder than study.
